chemistry_leaks.text: She looks you up and down like a delivery she's about to sign for. 'Ehen. Correct package.'
'Who does your hair? Send me their number. For business. And for me.'
'Is that outfit original or Balogun? Don't answer. I like it either way.'
'That beard is doing logistics for your whole face.'
'We'll fix the outfit. I know a guy in Balogun. Two guys.'
She silences all three phones. At once. For you.

phone.text: Hi, it's Mercy 😊 Account number below. For transport. Yes, before we meet. Logistics is logistics.

beats.text: Ojuelegba, rush hour. A dispatch bike cuts through three lanes of danfos and stops at your feet.
The rider pulls off her helmet. Braids, gold earrings, three phones buzzing in three different pockets.
You're the one. I'm late for four things, so you have ten minutes. Impress me.
One phone keeps ringing. She doesn't check who it is. She already knows.

locked_in.title: Head of Sales
locked_in.text: She took you to Benin to meet Mama. Mama asked for your surname and your blood group. Merci Luxe has a glass door now, and your name is on the lease beside hers.

chief_sponsor.title: Out-Sponsored the Chief
chief_sponsor.text: Locked In. She blocked Chief on all three phones and returned the gold bracelet in a pepper soup flask. He still sends a Christmas hamper addressed 'To my daughter and the competitor'.

japa.title: Long Distance, Short Notice
japa.text: Locked In, across an ocean. She video-called you from Toronto arrivals in a puffer jacket: 'I've started your paperwork. Don't make me regret it.' You haven't. Yet.

quitting.title: The Last Stop
quitting.text: She quit every sponsor. Daddy Lekki sent one last voice note; she played it on speaker and laughed. Now it's suya on Fridays, Mama on Sundays, and you every day in between.

counter_con.title: Out-Hustled the Hustler
counter_con.text: You walked off with the bag before she could play you. Somewhere in Lekki, Mercy is telling Ivie, 'Respect.' From her, that's practically a love letter.

survived.title: Sponsor Number Four
survived.text: 'You're my person,' she says. 'For now.' Weekends are still dark, but Monday mornings, akara and pap, are yours.

chief_sponsor.text: 'You're my person. For now.' Monday mornings are yours. On Fridays, a tinted Prado still idles at the corner of her street.

quitting.text: 'You're my person. No for now.' She still flinches when a Prado passes. A bit less every week.

scandal.title: The Parlour's Favourite Triangle
scandal.text: Trending: 'Mercy's sponsor number four.' Ivie posted the receipts, the live clip and your face. Your aunty shared it with a Bible verse.

sapa.title: Invested in Logistics
sapa.text: You funded the bags, the bikes and the pop-up. You now own one helmet and zero naira. Mercy sent ₦5k 'for transport'. You took it.

breakdown.title: Ring Light Breakdown
breakdown.text: You cried on Mercy's live by accident. 4,000 viewers. She ended the stream, sat you down and made banga. It didn't fix anything. It helped.

ghosted.title: Delivered, Not Read
ghosted.text: All three phones went quiet at once. Last seen: Friday, 6:59pm. It's been Friday for three weeks.

fumbled.title: Fumbled the Quitter
fumbled.text: She quit her sponsors for you. You went through her phone, posted her business and called her a hustler in public. She was. She was also yours.

obsession.title: Obsession
obsession.text: You started tracking her phones, her Fridays, every Prado on her street. She stopped laughing around you. Watching someone isn't the same as keeping them. Control isn't love.

walked_away.title: Walked Away
walked_away.text: For once, you left first. Dispatch bikes still make you look twice. You don't follow them anymore.
